title: heic-support broken
author: MarqueeDOTscr
summary: Image Resizer regressed for HEIC files: it opens a file picker instead of using the selected Explorer item, and later reports indicate HEIC is no longer recognized at all.

confidence.rationale: The regression and shell-flow symptom are well established, but codec availability versus extension filtering must be separated in reproduction.

judgment.rationale: Multiple users report the same regression, and issue 47840 was explicitly closed as a duplicate of this canonical issue. The file-type activation/codec path can be reproduced by maintainers.
evidence: The original report says HEIC worked previously and regressed by PowerToys 0.97.1.
The context-menu action opens a file chooser; selecting the file manually previously allowed resize.
Later reports say HEIC files are not recognized at all, and issue 47840 was closed as a duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with and without the Windows HEIF extension, then inspect HEIC extension filtering and WIC decoder activation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The canonical issue is sufficiently concrete for a design candidate. The maintainer reproduction should first distinguish missing codec support from PowerToys incorrectly filtering or handing off a valid HEIC shell item.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore HEIC shell-item recognition in Image Resizer
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Image Resizer activation or decoder-eligibility path likely rejects .heic selections after a registration/filter change, causing file-picker fallback or no processing despite an installed HEIF decoder.
plan: Compare HEIC extension/codec eligibility and shell activation handling with a supported format and the last known working behavior.
Treat a valid selected HEIC shell item as input when a WIC decoder is available and surface a clear codec requirement when it is not.
Add tests for extension normalization, decoder availability, multi-select activation, and no-codec error handling.
verification: Invoke Image Resizer from Explorer on HEIC files with the HEIF extension installed and confirm the selected files reach the resize dialog directly.
Repeat without a decoder and verify an actionable error rather than an unrelated file picker.

confidence.rationale: The regression and shell-flow symptom are well established, but codec availability versus extension filtering must be separated in reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Image Resizer regressed for HEIC files: it opens a file picker instead of using the selected Explorer item, and later reports indicate HEIC is no longer recognized at all.
known_information: The problem is specific to .heic while other Image Resizer formats continue through the normal dialog.
No active fix or assignee is linked.
inferences: A file-type registration/filter change or failed WIC decoder selection may cause the selected shell item to be rejected and fall back to file-picker flow.
issue_context.analysis: The canonical issue is sufficiently concrete for a design candidate. The maintainer reproduction should first distinguish missing codec support from PowerToys incorrectly filtering or handing off a valid HEIC shell item.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and all comments.
Inspected issue 47840 and confirmed a collaborator closed it as a duplicate of 45474.

reproduce.title: Compare HEIC context-menu activation with decoder present and absent
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build

setup: Prepare one HEIC and one JPEG in the same folder.
Record whether the Windows HEIF extension is installed.
steps: Right-click the HEIC and select Resize with Image Resizer.
Record whether a file picker or resize dialog opens and whether the selected file is present.
Repeat the HEIC test after changing only HEIF decoder availability if practical.
